description: RAVEL guidance for writing and reviewing a Rivet routine from a paper. Each checklist item names the definition or convention to verify against the paper and the analysis specification.
authoring: Name the analysis class, the RIVET_DECLARE_PLUGIN argument and the routine name exactly as routine_name.
Declare every projection in init(); apply projections in analyze().
Book a histogram for a HEPData table with book(h, d, x, y) or book(h, "dNN-xMM-yKK"), using only identifiers listed in hepdata_tables; the binning then comes from the reference file.
Book a histogram with explicit edges only when the record has no table for it, and take the edges from the paper or the analysis specification.
Fill a per-event observable once per event; for an observable defined per object, state that in a comment.

Apply the normalization the normalization_contract states in finalize(): xsec means crossSection() over sumOfWeights() in the stated unit; fiducial_N and in_range_N mean unit area over the stated range.
For a one-dimensional slice of a two-dimensional distribution, divide by the slice width when the contract basis is bin_width_area_2D.
Where analysis_spec marks a field ambiguous or not_specified, implement the reading the specification records and name it in a comment; do not invent a value.

checklist.check: Leptons are dressed or bare as the paper defines, with the stated dressing cone and photon source.
Leptons from hadron decays are excluded and leptons from tau decays are included or excluded as the paper states.
Jet inputs exclude neutrinos and the dressed leptons (and photons) the paper removes; jet algorithm, radius and thresholds match.
Overlap removal uses the paper's order, distance definition and thresholds.
Lepton, jet and b-tag vetoes use the paper's thresholds and acceptance.
Every fiducial cut in the paper is applied once, in the stated order, on particle-level objects.
Missing transverse momentum is built from the stated invisible particles or from the visible-object recoil, as defined.
Reference frames, boosts and object pairing (for example neutrino solutions or lepton pairing) follow the paper, with one choice per event.
Each per-event histogram is filled once per event; no loop fills the same histogram for several candidates or solutions.
finalize() applies the stated basis: cross section over sum of weights, unit area, or raw counts, including overflow handling.
The cross-section unit (pb or fb) and per-unit-variable densities match the HEPData table.
Slices of a 2-D distribution use the stated slice edges and divide by the slice width where the published values are double-differential.
Every booked table identifier exists in the HEPData record and its binning comes from the record.
Projections are declared in init() with stable names and applied, not constructed, in analyze().
Fills use the event weight handling of the Rivet version in use; no manual weight is applied twice.
